messages:
incident-bot: :bell: Pager INC-4897 — EU-West generation p95 spike (p95 > 400ms for 5m). Alert rule: gen_latency_p95_eu-west. Please acknowledge.

priya: acked. i'm primary for the shift, taking lead. quick blamestorm: ingress routing shows uneven traffic, a few hosts at CPU 98% and kernel softirqs high. suspect network packet steering regression after last kernel upgrade.

marcus: joining. i'm seeing 5 hosts (model-host-12..16) with heavy softirq and packet drops in dmesg. kube-proxy conntrack counts climbing. also a small but growing error spike (502) for some customer requests.

julia: ops on-call here. Customers possibly affected: phoenix.ai (prod), inkwell-studio (prod), test-swarm (dev). no pages from customers yet but monitoring their dashboards.

priya: immediate mitigations i want to try: 1) reduce per-host load by modifying routing weights to prefer warm pool hosts 2) cordon+drain one host at a time for kernel restart and nic reset 3) enable fallback multi-region routing to eu-central for new connections. applying weight change now.

ops-bot: Command run by priya: ```routerctl adjust-weights --pool eu-west-serving --weight-map "warm=0.6,warm-higher=0.4" --reason "INC-4897 reduce hot-hosts"```  applied.

marcus: starting cordon/drain on model-host-14. sequence: cordon -> drain pods -> restart network service -> uncordon. doing one host to avoid ripple. command: ```kubectl cordon model-host-14 && kubectl drain model-host-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data```

julia: i'll open a PS incident note for external comms and queue a short status page update if impact persists past 10m. draft: "Performance degradation affecting generation endpoints in EU-West; mitigation in progress."

priya: thanks. note on routing: fallback to eu-central will be enabled only for new sessions to avoid cold-start penalties. runbook pointer: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/network_latency_and_steering.md. Also see: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/drain_host_checklist.md for safe drain steps.

marcus: drain completed on host-14, restarted network stack, kernel bump reverted via hotfix. host back in service; cpu and softirq metrics normalized on host-14.

ops-bot: Host action log: host-14 drained and uncordoned by marcus at 2026-03-15T01:23:47Z.

priya: after first host maintenance p95 dropped from ~470ms to ~310ms. still some fluctuations. plan: continue rolling one host at a time (15 then 13), monitor for any regression. if p95 goes above 450ms for 3 consecutive minutes, trigger eu-central spill for new sessions.

rosa: noticed a backlog on request-queue service for batch_flush worker; opening ticket to temporarily reduce batch_window from 50ms to 25ms to lower tail latency. Command suggested: ```svcctl update request-queue --batch-window 25ms --scope eu-west --canary 0.2```

priya: approved for canary. rosa, apply canary then escalate if good.

rosa: applied canary 20% to request-queue batch_window=25ms. monitoring metrics. so far reduces p99 by a small amount in canary group.

julia: status page set to "degraded" for EU-West generation route. draft customer blurb posted to ops slack channel.

priya: handoff plan in 18m: i'm primary until 02:00Z, then julia will take over if stable. checklist for handover: - confirm p95 < 350ms for 20m - confirm host drain rotations completed for hosts 12..16 - confirm request-queue canary success and roll or rollback decision - ensure no new 502 spikes for phoenix.ai/inkwell-studio - keep eu-central spill permissive but not forced - keep routing weight changes in place until kernel hotfix rolled to all hosts.

marcus: one note for next shifter: kernel hotfix is queued for full rollout in maintenance window at 04:00Z; if you see reappearance of softirq after rollout, don't immediately open more hosts for drain — contact netinfra first.

ops-bot: Incident update: 01:28Z  p95 320ms, p99 540ms, errors slightly elevated (502+3%). Ongoing actions: rolling host maintenance, request-queue canary, routing weight adjustments.

julia: i'll be ready to take primary at 02:00Z. copying this thread into /handoffs/2026-03-15/eu-west-inc-4897.md and pinging @oncall-manager.

priya: leaving these pinned: runbook links, commands executed (routerctl, kubectl drain, svcctl), customer list, and ops-bot logs. i'll remain reachable as secondary. small ask to next shifter: if you decide to enable eu-central spill, update status page and post short customer note with expected latency impact.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: primary=julia, secondary=priya, started=2026-03-15T02:00:00Z. thread closed for handover. If new alerts trigger, reopen this thread."
